long_biography.plain_text:
Programming came early for American technology entrepreneur Mark Zuckerberg. He was writing software by middle school and studied computer science at Harvard, where he and fellow students launched Facebook in 2004 as a campus directory. Its rapid expansion led him to leave college and build the network full time. The growth of that platform made his founder stake the basis of his fortune.

Facebook later became Meta, with Zuckerberg continuing as founder, chairman and chief executive. He and Priscilla Chan also created the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, bringing engineering into biomedical science and education. Its research institutes, funding and software tools extend his early interest in building systems from connecting people to helping scientists understand disease.
